450.t: Theater work in London after the trio
450.s: After the trio she did theater in London, including Kennedy's Children and Three Penny Opera with Vanessa Redgrave.
450.q: I did some wonderful theater in London. I did “Kennedy’s Children” which is a wonderful play. I did Jenny, the betrayer in “Three Penny Opera” with Vanessa Redgrave. I’ve done all kinds. You know, if I couldn’t work anymore and couldn’t sing anymore, I could always go into the theater and be a…

450.t: The Threepenny Opera, Lotte Lenya and engagements to Vidal Sassoon and Lenny Bruce
450.s: Richardson persuades her to join The Threepenny Opera; she meets Lotte Lenya, recalls Richardson's parties, her engagements to Sassoon and Bruce, and the Establishment club.
450.q: the ground, white imitation fur. He said, “I’m so sorry I’m late, but I had a meeting and I was held up.” I said, “Well, I just got out of prison.” He took me in, filled a glass – a huge glass – with whiskey. He said, “I want you to be in my show.” I said, “I don’t want to do theater.” He said,…

450.t: Meeting Sean Lynch, Wham! Bam!, Cranks and marriage
450.s: She meets the actor Sean Lynch, tours in Wham! Bam! Thank you, Ma'am with Marty Feldman and Oscar Brown Jr., marries Lynch, and recalls the show Cranks.
450.q: guy in a leather jacket came up and said, “Are you Annie Ross?” I said yes. He said, “I love you.” I said, “Oh, thank you,” and off he went. I said to Fizz – was her name – I said, “Fizz, I just had the most lovely thing happen. A guy came up and said, ‘I love you’.” That was it. The next time I…

406.t: Playing tenor at Freedomland for Paul Lavalle, 1963
406.s: Paul Lavalle called him to play tenor at Freedomland, so he bought the tenor he still plays, and recommended drummer Sol Hall for the World's Fair.
406.q: Well, this comes next, 1963. I got a call that Paul Laval wanted a tenor player. Paul called me because I had worked with him in radio. We had become good friends, and he called me to come up and work with him at Freedom Land on tenor, so I bought a tenor. I didn't have one at the time.

406.t: The Poconos summers and the Ringling Brothers Circus at Madison Square Garden
406.s: From 1971 he worked Unity House in the Poconos each summer and Ringling Brothers at the Garden and Nassau Coliseum each spring and fall.
406.q: At the Unity -- Unity House, yes, Unity House. And then in the spring, every spring since '71 I've been doing Ringling Brothers Circus at the Garden when they come into the Garden. And we're getting ready to start it tomorrow out in Coliseum.

406.t: Becoming a Madison Square Garden house-band musician
406.s: Since 1971 he played ice shows and circuses in the Garden house band, getting in through trumpeter Renauld Jones and contractors Charlie Cotterson and Jack Shannon, and switched from baritone to tenor.
406.q: And then I went in '72 -- also went to Canada with Earl Hines playing at the Sauveron, you know, with his group. And now -- so that's -- now, the rest of the time since '71-'73 -- '71 up until now I've been on the house band at the Garden, play the ice shows, Holiday on Ice, Ice Capades, Moscow…

93.t: Filling in for George Hillman in Curly McDimple
93.s: Green says he formed the Hoofers; he took over the Bojangles role for two weeks in the off-Broadway musical Curly McDimple at the Bert Wheeler Theater for George Hillman.
93.q: Chuck and Chuckles. Well, he was pinch-hitting for a vacation -- a very dear friend of his, one of the brothers of the Hillman Brothers, you see and Chris's brother. His name was George, you know. George Hillman. And he was playing Bill Bojangles Robinson, you see. But he was only playing Bill and…

93.t: Celebrity audiences and the show renamed The Hoofers
93.s: At the Mercury Theater with celebrity audiences the show broke records and was renamed The Hoofers; Green mentions Derby Wilson.
93.q: Well, it really -- it became another sensation. It starts -- it broke its own record. You see, because people like Celeste Holms, Mrs. Hoot Gibson, Bert Wheeler, Bert Law's sister, you know, and Henny Youngman, Soupy Sales, see, Dorothy Townson and people like that was happening to be in these…

93.t: Timeline of the show and Rhythm Red's song
93.s: Green dates the Bert Wheeler run from 1966-67, then the Mercury; dancers drifted back to other commitments, Rhythm Red wrote Got to Go Tap Dancing Tonight, and they met Jack Bradley.
93.q: So, as a tap dancers got less and less, see, because now one of them had to go back to his school. He was a teacher. He had a school, and he had a student body. That was out white member was Jerry Ames. On -- see, because he took them out on tours, and they did some dances. You know, new dances,…

202.t: Jacques Brel show in the Village and keeping it simple
202.s: Subbing in the Brel quartet he played afterbeats in seven-eight; he says it is hard to be simple.
202.q: Yes. They had a little quartet down there. And Wayne Wright sent me in as a sub. And I got along all right. But there was seven-eight time and things like that you know. And the keyboard player didn’t play piano, he played all kinds of, what the hell they call it. The drummer was never, never just…

691.t: Off-off-Broadway show in a Bucks County barn
691.s: Overcoming not reading music, she auditioned for a Hair-like show rehearsed in a barn, late sixties.
691.q: Well I wanted to audition for theater for years, but I heard that you had to read music. And I did not read music. I didn’t study piano or sight singing. I started sight singing courses sometimes and then I’d drop out because I had to go somewhere out of town or whatever. And finally I got up…

692.t: Monterey concert version and renewed interest
692.s: The show never reached Broadway; Jimmy Lyons had them do a concert version at Monterey, and there is new interest in it as a period piece.
692.q: Well it never came about. Jimmy Lyons at the Monterey Jazz Festival telephoned us. We had moved to Connecticut by that time, and said “I want you do to it in Monterey.” Well of course it’s not a situation where you can mount a musical in Monterey. And so I decided okay, we’ll do it as a concert…

795.t: Guest bands, Brandi Carlile and in-ear monitors
795.s: Guest acts mostly bring touring bands; Gluck praises Brandi Carlile's unplugged set and explains how in-ears reduce leakage in SNL's fragile mixes.
795.q: It’s almost always touring. If someone has let’s say a bunch of horn players or they need a dozen strings then that will usually be a pick-up ensemble from the City. And you know, and in fact the music contractor we use, Sandy, who was the one playing violin in that thing, in that one story, I’ll…

796.t: After Gary Burton: Schoolhouse Rock and Mount Airy Lodge
796.s: Commercial work in New York, Schoolhouse Rock with Dorough, and a year with Bob Newman's band at Mount Airy Lodge where he met Steve Gilmore.
796.ch: Poconos and the Phil Woods era begins
796.q: Oh I was doing commercial work in New York, you know gigs and recordings, and working on the “Schoolhouse Rock” series with Bob and sometimes I played on, well the great preponderance of those tracks are me on drums.

588.s: She hated Las Vegas, was fired at Caesars Palace after singing Coltrane's 'Africa' lyric, and joked about being Lincoln's illegitimate daughter.
588.q: Hated it. Las Vegas is a place where people go who don't see themselves as creative. If you're creative, you're like in the manger. At Blues Alley, in the alley. Las Vegas is for show business. I went to Las Vegas, to Caesars Palace once and I went there with John Coletrain's Africa. I had written…

108.t: Back to Broadway shows after ABC
108.s: Within two weeks of the staff ending he plays Lorelei, Shenandoah, Timbuktu and Man of La Mancha.
108.ch: Miss America and the Goodman Russia tour
108.q: I did some of that, but I went back to the theaters. I went back and did Lorelei, the Carol Channing show. I did that, and I was working with one of my dear friends, Dick Perry, who was a first trumpet player. I did that show. Then what did I do? I did Shenandoah, and I did Timbuktu, the Eartha…

145.t: After Basie: George Rhodes, Sammy Davis and the Now Grove
145.s: His first work after Basie was at the Coconut Grove with Sammy Davis's band, as contractor and lead saxophone, then freelance.
145.q: When I first left Basie, I think my first regular employment was working at the Coconut Grove with George Rhodes' (PHONETIC) band, Sammy Davis Group. That's when they reopened the Coconut Grove and called it the Now Grove. (PHONETIC). I worked there as a contractor for his band and lead saxophone…

382.t: 'My Old Friends': from La MaMa to Broadway
382.s: She got involved through Phil Rose; the show opened Off-Off-Broadway in 1978 and moved to a midtown theater, running April to May.
382.ch: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
382.q: Yeah. Well, I guess through the fact that I was doing "My Old Friends" two years ago. I got involved in this stage production. I got a call from some woman. Her name was Rosetta Reitz, I found out. She said there's a show going into rehearsal and there's a part in it for you. So she said if you're…

384.t: Sixties work, records and the Goldman Band
384.s: He was constantly called for Columbia record dates and was a steady with the Goldman Band, a marches-only outfit, while also playing snare in a Chambersburg band.
384.ch: Hutto 1978-79: family, favorites and record lists
384.q: Well that was more year around, they played nothing but marches, you know, the Goldman Band. And I was playing in the Chambersburg Band, snare drum at the same time. So I knew how to play....

386.s: He wishes the Langston Hughes work had been a musical.
386.q: No..mhm mhm. I had begged Langston...this was the forerunner of the Eubie and Don't Bother Me and all of that. I told Langston, "Langston, don't make this a play. Make it a musical." But I don't know if he had the say so, or if he was, you know, who had the rights to the book. But if they'd of made…
